gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured usable-energy or inverter idle-draw figure for any candidate. The Solar Lab measured AC efficiency and idle draw for three 2 kWh stations: ChatGPT's 'best overall' EcoFlow DELTA 3 Max at 79% and about 27 W, the Anker SOLIX C2000 Gen 2 at about 89% and about 18 W, and the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 at 94% and 9.5 W. Applied to the rated batteries, that is about 1,620 Wh usable on the DELTA 3 Max against about 1,950 Wh on the Elite 200 V2, roughly 20% more air-conditioner runtime from a battery of about the same size.
standout_why: I compared against the two cited pages. buyersheet.com/power-stations/best/window-ac/ says it 'compares portable power stations using manufacturer specs' and applies a flat 85% inverter efficiency to every model. generatorchecker.com/guides/window-ac-on-power-station/ applies a flat 0.70 derate plus estimated surge multipliers (1.5× and 3×), and says it cites no named test. Neither page gives a measured efficiency, usable Wh or idle-draw figure by a named reviewer, and neither shows that efficiency differs between models. I did not open the uncited results (stationhours, runtimemath, lightsonlab, homepowerfacts, poweroutlast, wattcrate, howlongwillitrun), so I have not checked whether any of them carries measurements. I rated this 2, not 3, because the DELTA 3 Max figure comes from one test with no byline or date, and The Solar Lab does not state its test conditions.
decides: In the 2 kWh tier, the measurements favour the BLUETTI Elite 200 V2 over ChatGPT's 'best overall' DELTA 3 Max. Two labs agree on the Elite 200 V2: The Solar Lab measured 94% efficiency and APH Networks drained 2,028 Wh (97.8% of rating) at about 987 W. The DELTA 3 Max measured 79% efficiency and about 27 W idle, the worst of the three. At an assumed 450 W (5,000 BTU) draw with no compressor cycling, that works out to about 4.3 h for the Elite 200 V2, about 4.05 h for the C2000 Gen 2 and about 3.6 h for the DELTA 3 Max. Idle draw adds to the gap because a window AC's compressor cycles off and the inverter keeps drawing. Over an 8-hour night that is about 216 Wh at 27 W against 76 Wh at 9.5 W. In the 3 kWh tier, Notebookcheck's Elite 300 test (88% at about 200 W, over 92% at 1,800 W) and The Solar Lab's idle figures (Elite 300 15 W, DELTA 3 Ultra 22 W with 82% efficiency) also lean toward BLUETTI. None of these labs ran an actual air conditioner, so the measurements cannot confirm or rule out compressor startup on any candidate.
